question.leadin: The half-brother of this country's leader was assassinated in the Kuala Lumpur airport in 2017.
question.text: Name this country, led by the hereditary Kim family dictatorship. Its capital city, Pyongyang, is home to Juche (joo-chay) Tower, built by its first leader, Kim Il-Sung.
question.answerHtml: North Korea [or the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea]
question.clue: This country diverged from traditional Marxism-Leninism with its Juche ideology.

swap.text: In the Battle of Incheon [in-CHAHN], MacArthur led a surprise amphibious assault on Korean troops, leading the way for the UNC to recapture this city.
swap.clue: The Han River runs through this city, and it shares an administrative region with Gyeonggi Province and Incheon.

question.leadin: After conducting "literati purges" against members of the Sarim faction, one emperor banned an alphabet used in this peninsula to suppress criticism of his regime.
question.text: Name this East Asian peninsula, once home to the kingdom of Joseon ["JOH-sun"]. This peninsula juts off of modern-day Russia and China and is separated from Japan by a namesake strait.
question.clue: The "Three Kingdoms" of this region included Baekje, Silla, and Goguryeo.

swap.text: Yi fought on behalf of this Korean dynasty that ruled from 1392 until Gojong was deposed by Japan's annexation of Korea in 1910.
swap.clue: As he died, a military leader of this kingdom instructed, "Beat my war drums. Do not announce my death."

question.text: The creation of turtle ships is credited to this dynasty's Admiral Yi Sun-Sin. This dynasty's Sejong the Great developed the notable Hangul script, which is still used today.
question.clue: Members of the yangban (yong-bon) class were killed by followers of the "Eastern Learning" Donghak religion during this dynasty.

swap.leadin: According to the Samguk sagi, this kingdom was founded by Jumong, whose wife headed south to found the Baekje kingdom.
swap.text: Name this northernmost of the 3 kingdoms of the peninsula which now bears its name, along with Baekje and Silla. At its peak part of this kingdom extended into Manchuria and Siberia.
swap.clue: Some of the best-preserved art of this kingdom survives in the tomb of Dong Shou at a complex at Anak.

question.text: The turtle ship was designed by this Korean admiral to repel invasions. After his death at the Battle of Noryang, his nephew wore his armor and beat his war drum to keep morale high.
question.clue: This man's alliance with Ming China led to the end of the Imjin War and the Japanese retreat from Busan.

swap.text: This Joseon king developed hangul and encouraged the development of scientific technology. He is the only king of Joseon with the appellation "the Great."
swap.clue: This king implemented the Hall of Worthies, which produced a replacement to Hanja that only has 28 letters.

question.text: China's civil service exam was imitated by the gwageo, an exam popular during this empire. Chogye Buddhism flourished in this kingdom, which was founded by Taejo and fought a series of wars against the Khitans.
question.clue: Twenty-nine women from hojeok ("HO-juck") families were married to this dynasty's founder, Wang Geon ("gun").

swap.leadin: This region was the site of Operation Paul Bunyan, which destroyed a politically explosive tree stump that precipitated the Axe Murder Incident.
swap.text: Identify this region whose center is home to the Bridge of No Return and which was circumvented several times by assassins intent on assaulting the Blue House.
swap.answerHtml: The Korean Demilitarized Zone [prompt on “South Korea-North Korea border” or equivalents]
swap.clue: Prisoner exchanges happen across the Bridge of No Return in this region, and its Joint Security Area features several blue houses for diplomatic meetings.

question.text: This man led North Korea during the Korean War. Despite dying in 1994, he continues to hold the title of "Eternal President" of North Korea.
question.clue: He agreed to the release of the crew of the Pueblo at Pammujan in 1968.

swap.text: In 1866, the American steamer General Sherman attempted to emulate Perry's expedition by visiting this non-Japanese East Asian city; however, the ship was destroyed by this city's residents. The USS Pueblo was captured off the coast of this capital city, and is still held in this city today.
swap.clue: Nationalists deny that the Han Lelang ("luh-lahng") Commandery took this city from the Yan ("yen") general Wiman.

question.text: Confucianism in Korea built upon earlier hierarchies such as the bone-rank system, which was used by this kingdom. This kingdom unified Korea in the 7th century after defeating its rivals Baekje and Goguryeo.
question.clue: This kingdom was ruled by the Gyeongju Kim clan for nearly 1000 years, making it one of the longest-surviving dynasties in history. Its aristocrats were called "sacred bone" or "true bone".

swap.leadin: Congressman Larry McDonald died aboard this flight, whose black box tapes were later released by Boris Yeltsin.
swap.text: Name this passenger flight that was shot down by a Soviet jet after accidentally crossing into Soviet airspace en route to Seoul from New York over fears that it was an American spy plane.

question.text: In the initial phase of the war, North Korean forces pushed UN troops back to this feature, named for a very southern Korean city. The so-called "Bowling Alley" was one segment of this feature.

swap.text: Under Yang, China attempted to conquer this kingdom, which opposed Baekje and Silla during the Korean Three Kingdoms Period. That invasion failed after the Battle of the Salsu River.
swap.clue: This first native Korean state arose near the Yalu River in the first century CE and conquered the Chinese colony of Lolang.

question.text: The Unifed Silla employed this caste system to divide up the aristocracy using a measure of closeness to the throne. This system determined everything from the color of clothing worn to the maximum allowed size of the home.

swap.text: Qing forces were supported by this Korean dynasty, which was founded by Yi Seonggye after the fall of the Goryeo and lasted until it was conquered by the Empire of Japan.
swap.clue: Admiral Yi Sun-sin successfully defended this kingdom from two Japanese invasions.

question.leadin: The Hanjungrok ("hahn-joong-rohk") memoirs written by Lady Hyegyeong ("hyay-gyong") are often used as evidence that an event involving Hyegyeong's husband and this object was not the result of a deep conspiracy.
question.text: Name this object. King Yeongjo trapped Crown Prince Sado in this object for seven days until he died of dehydration.

swap.leadin: This man constructed the Jongmyo shrine and the Namdaemun gate.
swap.text: Identify this founder of the Joseon Dynasty.
swap.clue: After defeating Singeom of Baekje, one ruler of this name occupied Hubaekje formalizing the unification of the the later three kingdoms in 936.
